sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was reduced significantly: FY26 EBIT guidance is USD -1.5bn to +1.0bn, compared to FY25 EBIT of USD 3.5bn (which was at the upper end of prior guidance). Management explicitly cites industry overcapacity and Red Sea reopening scenarios as headwinds. The share buyback was reduced from USD 2.0bn to USD 1.0bn, reflecting a more cautious approach. The tone is defensive about the near-term outlook, with emphasis on cost discipline and weathering a downturn.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue USD 13.3bn, down 8.7% YoY (from USD 14.6bn). FY25 revenue USD 54.0bn, down 2.7% YoY (from USD 55.5bn).
summary.eps: Not disclosed. Earnings per share for FY25 is USD 6,232m net profit / shares outstanding not given. Underlying profit for FY25 is USD 6,095m.
summary.guidance: FY26 underlying EBITDA USD 4.5bn to 7.0bn; underlying EBIT USD -1.5bn to +1.0bn; FCF ≥ USD 3bn; global container volume growth 2-4%; Maersk to grow in line with market. Capex FY26-27 combined USD 10-11bn.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 EBIT margin 0.9% (down from 14.0% in Q4 2024). FY25 EBIT margin 6.5% (down from 11.7% in FY24).
key_risks: Industry overcapacity from new vessel deliveries
Potential full Red Sea reopening in 2026, which would add further capacity
Ongoing freight rate decline (Ocean rates down 23% YoY in Q4)
Trade tensions and tariff environment impacting US-China volumes
Labour inflation and FX impact in Terminals
Logistics & Services still below 6% EBIT margin target
key_opportunities: Gemini network delivering cost savings of USD 820-1,100m annually
Terminals record performance with 20% revenue growth and 31% EBIT growth in FY25
Logistics & Services margin improvement (4.8% FY25 vs 3.6% FY24)
Strong balance sheet with net cash of USD 2.9bn to weather downturn
Continued share buyback program of USD 1.0bn and dividend of DKK 480/share

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: CEO Vincent Clerc states: 'The lower level reflects the higher level of uncertainty and the lower rate environment that we are headed into in 2026.' The tone is defensive about near-term headwinds while acknowledging operational progress.
